item.description: Texas Longhorns running back Michael Terry III (11) indicates a first down in the fourth quarter of the Longhorns' win over Mississippi Rebels 34-27 at Royal-Memorial Stadium in Austin, Oct. 24, 2026. (Sara Diggins/Austin American-Statesman) While preparing for this weekend's trip to play LSU, members of the Texas football team had plenty of questions to answer during Monday's meeting with the media. What kind of challenges can LSU present on defense? Is it hard for an out-of-state school to recruit the Louisiana prospects that LSU also wants? What's up with senior quarterback Arch Manning's facial hair ? On Monday, the Longhorns were also asked questions about colors. More specifically, orange and pink were topics of conversation. When they take the field at Tiger Stadium, the Longhorns will do so while wearing their burnt orange jerseys. Like most teams, Texas normally wears white when it plays in true road games and the program's all-white uniform - also known as the "icy white" look - has become a matter of pride. According to UT senior associate athletics director John Bianco, the Longhorns were last seen in orange for a road game when they opened the 1971 season with a 28-10 win at UCLA. item.title: Fabrizio Romano gives detailed update on that Alvarez-Zubimendi swap talk
item.description: Fabrizio Romano gives detailed update on that Alvarez-Zubimendi swap talk There has been considerable speculation in recent weeks about a potential swap deal between Arsenal and Atletico Madrid involving Martin Zubimendi and Julian Alvarez. The proposed arrangement appears straightforward, with Arsenal interested in signing Alvarez and Atletico Madrid reportedly keen to bring Zubimendi to their squad . Such an agreement could theoretically allow both clubs to secure players they want without pursuing separate transfers. However, the willingness of the players themselves remains a major obstacle. During the summer, Alvarez made it clear that he was not interested in joining Arsenal, despite the Gunners’ efforts to secure his signature. The Argentine reportedly wants to move to Barcelona, although Atletico Madrid would be unwilling to sell him to their Spanish rivals. Meanwhile, Zubimendi has spent much of this season on the Arsenal bench, prompting Atletico to consider whether they could bring him to Madrid and offer him a different situation. Despite that interest, the midfielder remains committed to Arsenal. The situation therefore involves two players who are not particularly interested in changing clubs or joining the teams reportedly pursuing them. Romano addresses Arsenal and Atletico rumours Transfer journalist Fabrizio Romano has now discussed the speculation surrounding the two players and dismissed suggestions that negotiations are taking place between the clubs. Speaking on his YouTube channel , he explained that there is currently no agreement being discussed and that neither side is working towards an exchange involving Alvarez and Zubimendi. He said: “First point, at the moment there are no negotiations ongoing between Atletico Madrid and Arsenal. “Second point, they are not working on a swap deal with Alvarez and Zubimendi. “Third point, Zubimendi has clarified that he’s not desperate to leave Arsenal and also Atletico Madrid are not going to invest 65, 70, 80 million on Martin Zubimendi in January.” (Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images) A January swap deal looks unlikely Romano’s comments suggest that the proposed arrangement is not currently being pursued by either club. Zubimendi is not pushing to leave Arsenal, while Atletico Madrid are also unwilling to spend the amount required to sign him during the January transfer window. Alvarez’s reported preference for Barcelona creates another complication for Arsenal, as the forward has previously shown little interest in moving to the Emirates. For now, the suggested swap remains speculation rather than an active transfer negotiation. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ ADMIN COMMENT So here are some simple rules which I must insist commenters follow…. item.title: Arch Manning gets his own Texas Longhorns bobblehead ahead of LSU game
item.description: The National Bobblehead Hall of Fame and Museum, an official licensee of the University of Texas at Austin, is producing the special-edition bobblehead with Manning. (National Bobblehead Hall of Fame and Museum) Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning has new hardware to add to his mantel. On Friday, Nov. 13, Manning's official bobblehead will be unveiled. The National Bobblehead Hall of Fame and Museum , an official licensee of the University of Texas at Austin, is producing the special-edition bobblehead with Manning. According to the National Bobblehead Hall of Fame and Museum, the Manning bobbleheads are now available for pre-order and are expected to ship in April. Each bobblehead will be individually numbered, with only 2,026 available. The bobbleheads cost $40 each, plus a flat-rate shipping charge of $8 per order. Manning will stand on a circular turf-like base bearing his name, the smiling Manning bobblehead wears a burnt orange No. 16 jersey and white pants. As the season gets closer to the College Football Playoff, Manning has more accomplishments to check off his list. Manning threw his 50th career touchdown pass against Mississippi State and followed that with three more scores in UT's 34-20 win at No. 19 Missouri last Saturday. On Nov. 14, Manning and the Longhorns take on LSU in his home state of Louisiana. Manning said Monday that playing LSU is just another game for him and the Longhorns. "I really don't have any legacy, you know, I have no family that went to LSU," Manning said. "I'm from New Orleans, which is an hour from Baton Rouge. So there's no real, there's no connection, really. It's not about me at all this week." The CFP Selection Committee released its second Top 25 rankings Tuesday night, with LSU falling seven spots from No. 14 to No. 21 following its 31-13 loss to Alabama. item.title: Dianna Russini’s one remark about women has allegedly ‘bothered’ people in NFL media
item.description: Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images Dianna Russini’s return to people’s screens has not come without criticism following her controversial offseason revelations involving the New England Patriots’ head coach, Mike Vrabel. The former reporter for The Athletic is now attempting to fly solo in the world of NFL media, having set up her own show in collaboration with a betting company. However, some of her comments made on her very first show have already sparked some frustration within the industry. Russini took little time to address her involvement with Vrabel, with the former reporter for The Athletic even making light of the situation. Although her comments on the memes she had seen were questionable at best, it is her comments on being an inspiration to other women which have really left a sour taste in people’s mouths. “I really hope that I can be someone other women see: you can pick yourself up, get back in there and not be afraid,” Russini said. NFL media members hit back at Dianna Russini’s return after Mike Vrabel scandal Russini claimed her husband helped her through the scandal , as she now makes an attempt to return as an NFL insider. Her reputation has taken a beating over recent months, and it seems as if her latest comments have not helped her cause. “Based on the people I heard from since yesterday [Monday], Russini’s remark about being an inspiration to other women was what bothered most people in the industry. Women in sports already didn’t like her. That comment didn’t help,” said reporter Bobby Burack. It could be a difficult ask for Russini to return fully to the world of NFL media, given what has gone down over the last 12 months. It is clear that she has attempted to make light of her downfall in an attempt to brush it under the carpet, but some of her comments are seemingly worsening her reputation even further. Burack claims some of the women in the industry already did not like Russini. So, to hear her suggest she could act as an inspiration to others after what she had done will only insult her colleagues working in the field. item.title: “You Will Rue The Day!” – Fans Taken Aback by Marta Kostyuk’s ‘Hoping For Double Fault’ Admission After Coco Gauff Loss At WTA Finals
item.description: Coco Gauff - US Open | © Imagn Numerous tennis fans were surprised to hear that Marta Kostyuk was hoping for a double fault from Coco Gauff during their round-robin clash at the WTA Finals on Thursday. Gauff beat Kostyuk 6-4, 7-5 in their final round-robin match. The American trailed the Ukrainian 5-1 in the second set as she struggled with a back issue. Gauff was plagued by double-fault issues, but mounted a stirring fightback and eventually turned things around. After the match, tennis journalist Christian Basnight interviewed Kostyuk, who admitted that she was hoping Gauff would gift her the set as she too was dealing with injury issues. “I was hoping for Coco’s double fault because she was double faulting a lot in that second set. My wrist started to hurt a lot in the first set, and then in the beginning of the second set, I wasn’t sure how much longer I can play. I couldn’t even hit the ball properly anymore. Coco deserves to win, she’s an amazing player.” Tennis fans reacted to Kostyuk’s comments on X (formerly Twitter): “I was hoping for her DF…you will rue the day Marta!” Jessica Pegula’s win denies Coco Gauff passage to the semifinals of the WTA Finals Coco Gauff would have advanced to the last four of the year-end championships had compatriot Jessica Pegula lost her final round-robin match against Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova. However, Pegula produced a gritty display of her own, downing her Czech opponent after saving a match point. The result ensured that Gauff will play no further part at the 2026 WTA Finals . Gauff finishes the 2026 season with one singles title: the Cincinnati Open . Gauff is set to represent the USA at the 2026 Billie Jean King Cup Play-offs. The USA will face Hungary in Delray Beach, Florida, later this month. item.title: Kyle McCord once stunned Miami. Now he's leading the Dolphins
item.description: MIAMI GARDENS ― Two years ago, the Syracuse Orangemen were trailing the Miami Hurricanes 21-0 in a November game at a dome in central New York. But Syracuse quarterback Kyle McCord would come alive. "He never batted an eye, never flinched," said Nunzio Campanile, then the Syracuse quarterbacks coach. "He just kept competing. Honestly, that was probably the best win in Syracuse in the last 20 years." McCord will make his first NFL start for the Miami Dolphins on Sunday at another dome, Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. Two years ago, McCord passed for 380 yards and three touchdowns in Syracuse's 42-38 comeback win . The 'Canes entered that game ranked No. 6. "I mean, that was probably the favorite game from my college career," McCord recalled. "Being able to go out like that and beat a great Miami team was a lot of fun. So now hoping to make those same fans happy instead of upset." McCord will have a least a four-game window to show Dolphins fans, and management, and coaches, what he can do. He'll be starting in place of Malik Willis (core injury), who is now on injured reserve. "He's super smart, very decisive, incredible hard worker, really accurate passer," said Campanile. "You know, he's aggressive. You know, he's not gun shy at all. And I think that, you know, he'll go out there and he's smart enough to understand how to manage situational football. And he's kind of ahead of his years." Nunzio Campanile is now offensive coordinator at UConn. His brother, Anthony, was a linebackers coach for the Dolphins from 2020-23. "Coaching him, I'm like, this guy's going to play for 15 years in that league," Campanile said of McCord. "You know, because he's, you know, he has the right demeanor, he has the confidence, he has the ability, and he just needs the opportunity." McCord is scheduled to face the Colts, Bills, Jets and Broncos. Miami (1-7) is about a field goal underdog at Indianapolis (2-7) on Sunday (1 p.m., CBS). "I would definitely say there's benefit to knowing you're playing beforehand and being able to get those live (practice) reps with the guys rather than kind of just being thrown into the fire without any reps of the ones," McCord said this week. "But I think regardless if it's a four-game stretch, a five-game stretch, a one-game stretch, whatever it is, I feel like you still approach it the same way. And you're not looking who we got next week and the week after that. I'm just focused on this Sunday." Miami coach Jeff Hafley believes McCord has some tools. "He's got a strong arm, stronger than you think," Hafley said. "He sees it well. The ball comes out fast. He's decisive. He's aggressive. I think you'll see as you get to know him, he has this kind of quiet confidence about himself. And I think one thing that you just take, he has experience." Dolphins offensive assistant Kevin Patullo said of McCord, whom he coached at Philadelphia last season: “He’s a good processor. He sees the field well. He’s a tough kid. He’s very professional.

item.title: “She Doesn’t Need To Be Protected”: WNBA Finals MVP Gabby Williams Weighs In on Caitlin Clark Debate
item.description: Gabby Williams Every hard foul on Caitlin Clark seems to spark a new debate over whether the WNBA is doing enough to protect its biggest star. Now, the league’s newest champion has weighed in. Golden State Valkyries forward Gabby Williams, the 2026 WNBA Finals MVP, spoke with CNBC’s Alex Sherman in a recent interview. Asked about the league’s relationship with Clark, Williams said the Indiana Fever guard carries a heavy burden but doesn’t need protection. Williams started by acknowledging the weight that comes with Clark’s spotlight. “ What Caitlin has to carry is probably very, very heavy ,” Williams said . Then came the part that stood out. Williams made clear that she sees Clark as a fighter, not a victim. “ I think she herself would be the first person to say that she doesn’t need to be protected. And I think she’s just as competitive ,” Williams said. Williams speaks from experience, having played against Clark. She said that competitiveness shows on the floor, and she does not believe Clark wants special treatment. “ I don’t think she asks for anything to be easy. None of us do. We’re all just athletes ,” Williams added. She also praised the way multiple women are now earning their praise, as well as the way the game is growing collectively. Williams led Golden State past Angel Reese and the Atlanta Dream, 4-3, in the first seven-game Finals in WNBA history, averaging 19.6 points, 3.6 rebounds, 2.7 assists and 2.6 steals along the way. The Valkyries became the fastest expansion team to win a title, doing it in their second season. Clark’s treatment has been a talking point since she arrived. Chennedy Carter drew a Flagrant 1 for a shoulder-check on Clark in June 2024, and Marina Mabrey shoved her in June 2025. Neither moment compares to the debate this past summer. On June 24, Phoenix’s Alyssa Thomas put a fist to Clark’s neck area during a loose-ball scramble. No foul was called. The league later upgraded it to a Flagrant 2 and suspended Thomas for one game with a $1,000 fine, while Thomas called it “ a complete accident. ” Fever coach Stephanie White blasted the no-call as “ absolutely unacceptable ,” “ egregious ,” and “ utterly disrespectful. ” WNBA legend Lisa Leslie added that “ the officials have got to do better. ” Fans reacted to Williams’ comments too. One fan urged Williams to recruit Clark to the Valkyries, writing, “ Come rescue her, please. ” The reaction shows how protective Clark’s supporters remain, even after hearing she does not want that label. item.title: Kiah Stokes Breaks Silence On Angel Reese Drama After WNBA Finals
item.description: Oct 19, 2026; San Francisco, California, USA; Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese (5) drives to the basket against Golden State Valkyries center Kiah Stokes (41) in the fourth quarter of game two of the 2026 WNBA Finals at Chase Center. Mandatory Credit: David Gonzales-Imagn Images Angel Reese’s trash talk followed her through the WNBA Finals, and by the end it had nearly become bigger than the games. The Golden State Valkyries won the title anyway. Now, someone from the winning side has spoken. Valkyries center Kiah Stokes, a four-time WNBA champion, addressed the chatter on Unsupervised, and her message to fans was simple: relax. Stokes started by thanking the supporters, then pushed back on how personally some have taken the Finals drama. “ I appreciate that we have a lot of fans. But sometimes I feel like y’all are taking things way too personal ,” Stokes said . She then explained how the locker room sees it. For Stokes, the exchanges were part of the game, and she has little interest in the outrage. “ Angel wanna talk s—, it is what it is. Like, it’s a game, and she was cooking ,” Stokes said. Stokes also pointed out that Golden State rookie Aminata Gueye talked back, and she loved it. “ Who doesn’t love this ,” she said. A lip-read clip from Game 2 showed Reese trading words with Gueye before a free throw. Reese had 30 points and 16 rebounds in Atlanta’s 79-65 win, and she was heard saying, “ You can’t guard me! ” Game 3 was the loudest. After the Dream’s 97-71 blowout, Reese hit the Valkyries’ bench with a “ You bum! ” and a pinching “ too small ” gesture. Before Game 4, she said she could “ take their confidence and just try to do whatever to mess them up. ” Then came Game 6, and Stokes was in the middle of it. Reese finished through contact against her , then told Golden State’s bench, “ Sit down, you’re on the bench. ” Atlanta won 80-69 to force a Game 7. The finale went the other way. Golden State won 68-63 at Chase Center behind Gabby Williams, who scored 28 of her 30 points in the second half. Reese grabbed 12 rebounds, but it was not enough to keep the “ too small ” gesture from coming back around. It was a painful finish for Reese, who helped Atlanta earn the No. 4 seed and reach the Finals in her first season with the Dream. Her trash talk was loud, but it came from a player who set a single-season record with 521 total rebounds. item.title: BSD Staff Predictions Roundtable: Minnesota
item.description: STATE COLLEGE, PA - OCTOBER 22: Theo Johnson #84 of the Penn State Nittany Lions catches a pass against the Minnesota Golden Gophers during the first half at Beaver Stadium on October 22, 2022 in State College, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images Penn State is on a winning streak after (somehow) beating Washington, and are back in the friendly confines of Beaver Stadium to take on Minnesota. How does the staff see this one playing out? Chris Penn State is fresh off another frustrating win, wherein they continued to show the inability to play 60 minutes of competent football. They’re back at home, but with the threat of foul weather looming, will it be enough against a Minnesota team not traditionally known for losing streaks coming off back-to-back losses? The offense and defense both produce stretches of competence, and learn to lean on the resurgent run game. But inevitably the 2-plus-quarter meltdown happens, and this time the team can’t overcome it. Minnesota 24, Penn State 17 Lando This is the kind of game where if Penn State’s offense was consistently explosve (as opposed to arbitrarily so), Penn State would have the slight edge against a tough Minnesota defense. However, I don’t think the Nittany Lions are able to run all over the Gophers the way they did in the first half against Washington. That combined with the fact they have yet to string together four straight good quarters since before conference play means the win streak comes to an end. Minnesota 21, Penn State 17 Tim Penn State might be playing with more confidence now that they’ve rattled off two straight wins in B1G play. I’m not sure what to make of a Minnesota team that upset Iowa, damn near upset Indiana, yet got waxed by Purdue, but it tells me that this game is also ripe for the taking. If the Lions can keep the Gophers ground game in check and force Drake Lindsey to have to throw it 30-plus times to beat them, then I like their chances. After all, Rashod Bateman ain’t walking through that door… Penn State 24, Minnesota 13 Colin Minnesota has been nearly impossible to figure out this year. The good news is they are one of the worst rushing teams in the country, averaging just 92 yards per game on the ground. The bad news is just under 4% of their dropbacks end in a sack, one of the best rates in college football. Penn State will need to find some semblance of a pass rush to get the Gophers’ offense off schedule. Penn State should have better luck passing the ball in this one, as Minnesota allows 7.5 yards per passing attempt. If the Lions can make a few chunk plays in the passing game, running lanes should open as the game goes on. This looks like a close matchup on paper, but give me Penn State at home to make the plays needed to win the game. Penn State 21, Minnesota 14

item.title: Surfing speedster Beardman gives a glimpse of Ashes future
item.description: Beardman was player of the match in the 2024 Under-19 World Cup final but has only played 26 matches in professional cricket across formats [Getty Images] How would you celebrate after posting record bowling figures on a debut aged just 21? If you're Mahli Beardman, now the most exciting fast bowler in Australian cricket, it's easy: "Try and get down to the beach!" In his maiden one-day international, which was also his first match for Australia on home soil, Beardman took 6-24 - the best figures by an Australian on a one-day debut. In doing so, the man who loves surfing swept aside England and set up a crushing victory in Perth. "I would love to live my life like him - pretty carefree, loves the ocean and loves to learn about fast bowling," beamed proud captain and fellow Western Australian Mitchell Marsh. With the nonchalance of youth and a flash of the future, Beardman was the perfect antidote during this moment of crisis for Australia. To him, sandpaper is merely used to clean up his surfboard. However, he has been made to wait for this moment and has had his troubles. Two years ago, and with only one professional match to his name, he toured England with Australia's white-ball teams after an impressive Under-19 World Cup. He did not play but bowling spells during intervals - his blond hair billowing behind him - felt like a glimpse into Australia and England's Ashes future. Watching Mitchell Johnson tear apart England in the 2013-14 Ashes inspired Beardman to take up cricket, while he has worked with Dennis Lillee, another Australian Ashes legend, since his teenage years. Add in accuracy, zip and effortless pace, and all of the ingredients appear to be there. But in 2025 he suffered the first of two stress injuries in his back – the scourge of the young fast bowler. The second of those came after his one previous Australia appearance to date – a T20 in Pakistan in January, in which he returned figures of 2-33. Two weeks earlier he had dismissed and unsettled Australia great Steve Smith in a Big Bash play-off match which had built momentum further. "There is always doubt," he said after his match-winning performance on Friday. "I don't think I ever lost my love for the game, it was more 'Will I come back and be able to bowl the same and will the air speed be there?'" After a carefully managed return, those questions were emphatically answered in Perth – where he has played all of his domestic cricket to date. Across 7.4 overs, Beardman averaged 86.5 mph – his quickest match on record. His fastest delivery was clocked at 90.6mph, again his best effort on record. Most impressive was his control of line and length, however. Rarely was there a ball there for England to hit. He moved the ball in and out, not a lot but enough – enough to find Harry Brook's outside edge for his first ODI wicket at the start of his second over. item.title: Dame Time is back in Portland — and the Blazers look dangerous
item.description: A new head coach will roam the sidelines. A franchise icon will make his long-awaited return. An All-Star will begin his redemption tour. And a new ownership group will watch its first season opener from Paul Allen’s former seats along the Moda Center baseline. The Blazers open the 2026-27 NBA season Wednesday night against the Phoenix Suns — a team they upset in April in the play-in tournament — and if you’re just now tuning in for the start of the regular season, well, there’s a lot you missed. RELATED: Suns vs. Blazers predictions, odds and best bets: Dame is home, and the model likes Portland on opening night Let’s catch you up. What does the starting lineup look like? The Blazers are expected to unveil a new starting lineup that features a pair of notable All-Star additions: Damian Lillard and Ja Morant . The backcourt duo is joining a fivesome that includes returning starters Deni Avdija , Toumani Camara and Donovan Clingan . It’s a versatile, star-studded lineup that features three All-Stars, a former All-Defensive Second Team selection, one of the best young centers in the NBA and loads of scoring potential. What about the rotation? item.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon’s loss at Illinois and firing of OC Drew Mehringer
item.description: CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — The Oregon Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) suffered their worst loss of the season at Illinois on Saturday . The 21-10 defeat came against a marginal Illinois team that started a true freshman at quarterback, rushed for 225 yards, and held Oregon to two scoring drives. As a result, on Sunday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning announced the firing of offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer . What that means for the rest of the season remains to be seen. Mehringer had to contend with several key personnel issues, including starting quarterback Dante Moore missing three games while in concussion protocol. Here are 10 takeaways from Saturday’s game and the firing of Mehringer: 1. It feels like Mehringer is the scapegoat in this mess Criticizing play-calling is an armchair quarterback’s delight, but doing so under Oregon’s current circumstances is somewhat obtuse. Few teams excel without their starting quarterback. The next factor is an offensive line that was clearly mismanaged in the offseason after losing three starters to the NFL. Next is inconsistent play from backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Then sprinkle in losing top wideout Jeremiah McClellan (broken foot) after three games, starting wide receiver Evan Stewart (undisclosed injury) for the last two games, and two more rotational wide receivers heading into Illinois. Does all of that excuse Mehringer for Oregon scoring just 42 points over the past three weeks? No. But those are a lot of obstacles for any offensive coordinator to overcome. Watch " Oregon football fires offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer " on YouTube Watch 2. Where does Lanning go from here? Lanning will probably announce his new offensive coordinator during his Monday press conference. He could promote from within to get through the season and then conduct a national search in the offseason. Or he may have someone in mind to take over now and beyond. Whatever Lanning decides, the next play-caller had better hope Moore returns, or little will change. 3. It could be time to add a veteran coach to the staff Lanning did well by hiring younger offensive coordinators, Kenny Dillingham and then Will Stein. But maybe it’s time to bring in an accomplished, seasoned veteran coach to add a new perspective to a relatively young staff. Someone with a track record of success as an offensive coordinator and maybe as a head coach. Someone like former Oregon coach Chip Kelly, Northwestern’s offensive coordinator. No, don’t expect Kelly to want to return to Oregon. But someone like him could fit perfectly. 4. The wide receiver situation After Saturday’s game, Raiola was asked twice how difficult it was to build timing with the receiving crew, which lacked McClellan, Stewart, and freshmen Messiah Hampton and Jalen Lott. item.description: The Oregon Ducks will face a team on Saturday with an even less desirable quarterback situation. Illinois (3-3, 1-2 Big Ten) quarterback Katin Houser suffered a broken hand that will sideline him for four to six weeks during a 38-37 overtime win over Michigan State on Oct. 10. Oregon has played its last two games without starting quarterback Dante Moore, who suffered a concussion in the second quarter of the Ducks’ 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. However, while Oregon can turn to junior Dylan Raiola — a Nebraska transfer with 23 career starts — and senior Brock Thomas, Illinois is relying on freshman quarterback Michael Clayton II, who will make his first start against the Ducks. A positive for Illinois is that Houser was injured before the team’s bye week, giving coach Bret Bielema two weeks to prepare Clayton. “It was just good timing,” Bielema told reporters during his Monday media session. Illinois is off to a disappointing start after going 9-4 in 2025 and 10-3 in 2024. The defense is below average, while the passing combination of Houser and wide receiver Collin Dixon is one of the nation’s best. Dixon is tied for third nationally with nine touchdown receptions. Illinois head coach Bret Bielema celebrates their overtime win over Michigan State as he walks off the field after an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026, in East Lansing, Mich. (AP Photo/Lon Horwedel) AP Photo/Lon Horwedel AP Photo/Lon Horwedel Now Illinois heads into Saturday’s game against a resurgent Oregon defense, trying to get Clayton up to speed. His performance against MSU elevated expectations. Houser left the game late in the third quarter with Illinois leading 23-10. Clayton completed 6 of 8 passes for 88 yards and two touchdowns. The final touchdown came in overtime on a 25-yard pass that put Illinois up 38-31. Sophomore quarterback Carson Boyd also played. He rushed once for seven yards but did not attempt a pass. Bielema and offensive coordinator Barry Lunney Jr. both said Boyd could play against Oregon (4-2, 2-1), but Clayton is the starter. Usually, Bielema said, his starting quarterback gets a lot of rest during the bye week while the staff works on player development. Given Clayton and Boyd’s inexperience, both got valuable reps in practice last week. “I think those two guys in particular took advantage of every rep,” Bielema said. Bielema has leaned heavily on transfer quarterbacks during his six years at Illinois, including Houser. But that could change if Clayton, a former three-star recruit, earns the job. “I’ve said several times that hopefully the next starter comes from within our program,” Bielema said. item.title: OSU's Legree leads nation in receiving as WSU clash looms
item.description: CORVALLIS — There may be no more appropriate way to describe Oregon State’s outrageously successful passing game this season than explosive. The Beavers lead the country in passing yards thanks in large part to 10 passes of 40-plus yards. Jesse Legree is responsible for eight of those catches, including all five of OSU’s 50-yard pass plays this season, making it no surprise that he leads the country in receiving yards and touchdowns entering this week’s matchup with Washington State. “You see him with ball in space, obviously taking the top off a number of times,” Washington State coach Kirby Moore said. “I think it’s about playing team defense. Obviously communication is going to be really important, where he’s at.” The Cougars (1-5, 0-2 Pac-12) have the No. 2 defense in the Pac-12 thus far and are having that success by keeping the top on their pass coverage. WSU has allowed 11 passes of 30-plus yards, which is tied for 129th nationally and nearly 10% of the passes it has allowed. However, opponents are not breaking through that mark often, with just four passes over 40 yards and none for more than 50, one of 30 teams yet to allow such a play this season. “We don’t want to let the verticals up,” Washington State safety Jaylen Smith said. “We take pride in (not) letting deep balls go. We always look to play top down and take away the deep routes first.” WSU defensive coordinator Trent Bray will be tasked with doing what nobody has been able to do yet this season: contain Legree. OSU offensive coordinator Mitch Dahlen has been creative in moving Legree around to prevent defenses from taking him away. Last week against San Diego State that included moving Legree into the backfield for a variety of plays. “People are going to try and hit him at the line of scrimmage,” Dahlen said. “They’re going to try and two-hand jam. If they’re going to try and two-hand jam, it’s like OK, how can I move this guy enough where you can’t do that? You put him in the backfield, unless you want to jump offsides and do it, you can’t do it that way. “That’s what we do a good job of as a staff, is moving him around where you can’t just put a safety over the top of him because if he’s in the backfield, what are you going to do there?” Even if the Cougars manage to limit Legree, the Beavers have shown they are more than capable of going elsewhere, with an outrageous 14 players catching passes last week. Aeryn Hampton (20 receptions for 245 yards) and tight ends Eric Olsen and DeCorion Temple each have at least 20 catches and Aaron Butler has four grabs for at least 20 yards. item.description: Liverpool title-winner set to return to Anfield in charity match James Milner Set for Anfield Return in Liverpool Legends Charity Match There are some players who leave a club, and some who leave a mark. James Milner belongs firmly in the second group, and Anfield will get the chance to welcome him home again when he lines up for the Liverpool Legends in this season’s charity match against Inter Legends. The game takes place on Saturday March 27, with a 3pm GMT kick-off, and it already has one proper pull. Milner is the first name confirmed for the home side, which feels fitting. He was never the loudest figure in Liverpool’s dressing room, but he was one of the most reliable, one of the toughest, and one of the men who helped drive the club back to where it belonged. Milner Return Brings Meaning Beyond Nostalgia Milner spent eight years at Liverpool after arriving on a free transfer from Manchester City in 2015. In that time, he made 332 appearances and played his part in one of the great modern eras in the club’s history. He helped the Reds win six major honours, including the Champions League in 2019 and the Premier League in 2020. He did it with a minimum of fuss and a maximum of graft. Wherever he was needed, he got on with it. Midfield, full-back, out wide, wherever. He gave Liverpool consistency, standards and a level of professionalism every squad needs if silverware is the target rather than a dream. Milner said: “I’m thrilled to have the chance to pull on the red shirt again and step back out at Anfield. It’s a special place, and playing there in front of the supporters is a feeling like no other. “What makes the legends match so special is that it’s about more than football. It’s a chance to give something back to the fans while supporting the work of the LFC Foundation. “I’m delighted to be the first to sign up and can’t wait to be part of it.” LFC Foundation Continues Powerful Community Work This fixture matters because the cause matters. The annual Liverpool Legends match has become a major part of the LFC Foundation fundraising calendar, and the numbers behind its work are striking. The 10 legends matches held so far have raised more than £10 million for communities across the Liverpool City Region and beyond. Last season alone, the Foundation supported 239,421 people, a rise of 65 per cent on the previous year. More than 50,000 additional participants were reached internationally, while the overall work created £96 million in social value. For every £1 spent by the Foundation, £10.53 was returned to the people it supports. Milner’s own charitable work has been tied closely to that effort. Since 2016, the James Milner Foundation has supported the LFC Foundation, helping more than 2,000 children enjoy safe and enjoyable activities during school holidays. item.title: Jim Brown, a coin flip and the decade that changed the Browns
item.description: EDITOR’S NOTE: We are observing the Browns’ 80th birthday with articles that define the franchise, one decade at a time. We began with their first decade — 1946-55 — and we continue by presenting 10 vignettes that shaped the run of 1956-65. As we continue our roller-coaster ride of the people and events that define Northeast Ohio's pro football team in 10-season blocks, we move to the team's second decade. The franchise's greatest quarterback has moved on, its greatest running back moves in and its greatest coach is asked to move out. Let's continue with the second 10 years, 1956-65, when the Browns bid farewell to legends and won their last NFL title. 1, The quarterbacks who tried to replace Browns legend Otto Graham Otto Graham was 34 when he retired in 1956, which seems rather young in an era when Tom Brady fired away at 44, and Aaron Rodgers, going on 43, plays on in Pittsburgh. Could Graham, great as he was as the quarterback of Cleveland's dynasty, have exceled in these times? Just as good a question: Could Brady and Rodgers coped in Graham's era? Equipment and rules didn’t protect quarterbacks, much. Graham plowed through most of his career in a plastic helmet with no face protection. A particularly brutal smash to his mouth in 1953 led to the invention of the face bar, changing the look of the game as the Browns entered their second 10 years. Rules subjected QBs to a more violent world than the one Patrick Mahomes and Josh Allen work in. When Graham decided that 10 seasons was gauntlet enough, the two-time, defending-champion Browns needed a successor in 1956. Head coach Paul Brown used three QBs in '56: Undersized Tommy O’Connell, a late draft pick of the Bears in 1952; journeyman George Ratterman, a Cincinnati Xavier High School alum who had backed up Graham, and Babe Parilli, a trade acquisition who once was a No. 4 overall pick by the Packers. All three played quite a bit in '56, combining for eight touchdown passes and 18 interceptions on a team that went 5-7. John Borton, a former Alliance Aviator and Ohio State Buckeye, became another option, but only ever played in one NFL game. 2, Cleveland lost a coin flip, wound up with Jim Brown Paul Brown wanted a quarterback upgrade in 1957, and had a high enough draft pick to possibly get one. The Steelers won a coin flip with the Browns (both teams were 5-7 in 1956) to determine who got the fifth overall pick. Two QBs Brown would have taken, John Brodie and Len Dawson, went to the 49ers and Steelers at No. 3 and No. 5. Cleveland's consolation prize at No. 6 was Jim Brown . Brown’s spent his entire pro career in Cleveland, from 1957-65. He retired after the '65 season, fresh off leading the NFL with 1,544 rushing yards (Chicago’s Gale Sayers was second with 867) and winning his third league MVP trophy. item.description: Liverpool, Bayern keep eye on German centre-back Liverpool are one of the clubs showing keen interest in VfB Stuttgart youngster Finn Jeltsch. The Reds are expected to bolster their defensive areas next summer, with the likes of Joe Gomez likely to be sold. Bayern Munich are also among clubs to have scouted the young central defender. Finn Jeltsch: Liverpool, Bayern eye move? View this post on Instagram The 20-year-old joined Stuttgart in the January window of 2025, and has made 62 appearances for them across all competitions. His impressive form did not go unnoticed, and has been picked up as back-up centre-back by Jurgen Klopp for the German national side. Christian Falk has exclusively told CFBayern Insider that Liverpool and Bayern Munich are among several top clubs to have scouted the German young talent. Virgil van Dijk is not getting younger, and the Reds must plan for his long-term replacements at some point. The Reds have Jeremie Jacquet and Giovanni Leoni as two fantastic young defenders, but Andoni Iraola would love to add a versatile young defender as well, and Jeltsch fits the bill. Liverpool scouts have watched him recently, and they are expected to monitor him in the upcoming games as well. We reported earlier that Bayern are interested in Tomás Araújo , and Falk has confirmed they are also interested in the young defender. Falk said: “It is TRUE: Liverpool have scouted VfB Stuttgart centre-back Finn Jeltsch. All the top clubs, including Bayern Munich, are scouting him. He was in the squad for Klopp first as a backup for the right-back. Then one of the central defenders became injured, and now he’s also the backup at centre-back. “This shows he can play many positions, and everyone can see the 20-year-old’s potential. Such players really are a present to everyone. Jeltsch is young, talented and can play many positions, and he’s not so expensive! Bayern Munich has an eye on him. “Last week, we mentioned that Tomás Araújo is on the list, and so is Jeltsch. He’s also on the list for many clubs in the Premier League. (Photo by Christian Kaspar-Bartke/Getty Images) Falk suggests that the youngster is unlikely to move to the Premier League as yet, rather he would want to progress steadily. He is doing a fantastic job at Stuttgart, and Bayern could be his next major step. The youngster has a contract at Stuttgart until 2030, and they are under no pressure to sell him immediately. item.title: Browns vs. Texans: Week 10’s matchup could decide the 2026 season’s direction
item.description: With the bye week looming, the Cleveland Browns return home after a strenuous road trip. The team has had some highs and many lows this season, but for the first time since 2023, they’re playing somewhat meaningful games in the middle of the season. Sunday’s tilt with the Houston Texans will be the first of four straight at home, but this matchup feels more important than the previous ones and is set to impact playoff odds greatly . If you were to ask who’s the biggest disappointment of the season so far, it would be the Texans (or the Los Angeles Chargers). Going into the season, many experts had this team penciled in as a favorite to represent the AFC in the Super Bowl. Considering the talent on both sides of the ball, an argument could be made that they are better than last year’s roster. It hasn’t been anything close to that. Considered one of the best in the league, Houston’s defense has been anything but. Overall, the unit has been a disappointment. Their run defense has been leaky, and they have been vulnerable to giving up explosives in the passing game. The Texans defense looked better last weekend against the Chargers, but anyone can have a get-right game against the winless LA team. The Texans haven’t looked like contenders at all this season. The defensive regression has more to do with their scheme not evolving, and the team is prone to letdown performances. Offensively, Houston appears to be clicking at a high level. Quarterback CJ Stroud has pretty much played himself into a new contract extension. While the Texans are essentially in playoff mode, the Browns are somewhat entering it. With the team at 5-4, going into the bye week with a 6-4 record could be big. Cleveland will probably not be favored in any of their games for the remainder of the season, but their schedule is somewhat favorable. Could the Browns beat the Texans this Sunday? Yes, but they are also prone to getting blown out if they aren’t careful. Sunday’s game against the Houston could be as close to a playoff atmosphere for Cleveland, and it will be interesting to see how they look. item.title: ‘So bad’: Jeff Teague says the New York Knicks should get rid of one player right away
item.description: Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images The New York Knicks came into the new NBA season with high expectations, but things haven’t fully gone to plan. The defending champions have lost five of their first 11 games, and although there have been some positives to take, there are quite a few problems as well. One such negative is the form of Mikal Bridges. Jeff Teague tells the New York Knicks to ‘move on’ from Mikal Bridges Bridges played a significant role in the New York Knicks’ road to winning the NBA Championship last season. The 30-year-old was not the superstar of the team, but he contributed heavily and was a key member of the roster throughout. However, this season, Bridges has really struggled, and his stats compared to last season have gone down significantly. Jeff Teague has watched Bridges’ performances this year, and after comparing his numbers to last season, he thinks the Knicks should get rid of him. He said on the Club 520 Podcast : “Yeah, it’s time to move on. It’s just like so bad. I’ve never seen nobody go from this (last season’s stats) to this (this season’s stats), and still be a starter. “Have y’all ever seen that drastic of a drop-off, though? I’m just saying, it’s Game 11, right? After five games, a good starter, five or six games, you will see him have like a 15-25 point night.” The Knicks really do have a problem with Bridges, for whom they surrendered four unprotected first-round picks, a first-round pick swap, a protected first-round pick and a second-round pick when they traded him from the Nets. The champions also gave him a four-year contract extension worth around $150 million, which is another reason why his performances are being judged so heavily. It remains to be seen what the Knicks will do now, but if his performances don’t improve, it will be difficult to justify keeping him. item.title: Confirmed: Barcelona complete €300 million financing deal to accelerate Spotify Camp Nou redevelopment
item.description: Confirmed: Barcelona complete €300 million financing deal to accelerate Spotify Camp Nou redevelopment Barcelona have officially confirmed that the club has completed a €300 million financing operation to support the remaining construction work at Spotify Camp Nou, providing fresh financial backing for the club’s ambitious Espai Barça project. The transaction has received approval from Spain’s National Securities Market Commission (CNMV), with Goldman Sachs acting as the sole placement agent. The additional funding forms part of Barcelona’s effort to bring the stadium redevelopment to completion after construction delays and an expanded project scope increased the financial requirements. It is to be noted that the club’s general assembly in September 2026 had already approved the €300 million project financing alongside a separate €210 million media notes operation. Barcelona secure fresh funding to complete Camp Nou The €300 million operation will support the transformation of Spotify Camp Nou, the centrepiece of Espai Barça. The club’s statement explained the ambition behind the project: “This funding will enable progress on transforming the Spotify Camp Nou, the centrepiece of Espai Barça, which will see it become the largest capacity football stadium in Europe, with an extensive offer of premium and hospitality spaces,” read the official statement from the club. The renovated stadium is planned to accommodate approximately 104,600 spectators, alongside 9,500 VIP seats and an expanded hospitality offering. It is to be noted that the financing is structured through the stadium’s existing securitisation framework, with repayment linked to future revenues generated by its operation. This includes income from premium hospitality and other stadium-related activities. Spotify Camp Nou targets completion in 2028 The current plan is to complete the stadium during the first half of 2028, with the roof installation scheduled for the summer and autumn of 2027. Barcelona have secured a €300 million funding boost for the Spotify Camp Nou project. (Photo by Pedro Salado/Getty Images) Barcelona are preparing for a return to the stadium in January 2028, although the full redevelopment will take longer. The venue has already secured a major international event, with UEFA selecting Spotify Camp Nou to host the 2029 men’s Champions League final . Barcelona and local authorities are also pursuing opportunities to bring further major competitions to the stadium, including a potential role in the 2030 men’s World Cup. Ultimately, the financing is not just about completing construction. Rather, Barcelona are investing in a stadium designed to generate greater matchday and hospitality revenue, strengthen the club’s commercial position and become one of European football’s leading venues.

item.title: National team coach to meet with Flick to discuss Barcelona defender’s fitness amid growing concerns
item.description: National team coach to meet with Flick to discuss Barcelona defender’s fitness amid growing concerns According to reports relayed by SPORT , Denmark coach Brian Riemer is planning a visit to Barcelona to meet Hansi Flick and discuss Andreas Christensen’s physical condition as concerns grow over the defender’s ability to regain consistent fitness. The report suggests that the meeting will focus on establishing a joint recovery plan that will allow the Barcelona defender to return to his best level without risking further setbacks. Christensen’s fitness becoming a concern Christensen’s repeated injury problems have disrupted his continuity over recent seasons, creating concern both at Barcelona and within the Danish national team. The defender played only 18 games throughout last season for Barça, while he has been unavailable for four matches in the ongoing campaign already. With Denmark, the seasoned campaigner was unavailable for the matches in March, but played twice during the summer, before missing the games during the last international break in September-October as well. Christensen’s injuries remain a concern. (Photo by Daniela Porcelli/Getty Images) As such, Denmark boss Riemer wants to meet with Flick and discuss the next steps in the defender’s recovery and how both sides can coordinate their approach. The meeting comes after Christensen returned to action against Atletico Madrid last Sunday, playing close to 30 minutes in the team’s 2-1 win at the Riyadh Air Metropolitano. Riemer wants a joint plan of action Flick’s decision to bring Christensen back against Atletico Madrid attracted some criticism in Denmark, even as he was left out of the national team squad by the manager for the current international break. Riemer’s intention is not to rush the 30-year-old back into the Denmark squad. Instead, the national team coach wants the defender to complete his recovery properly before returning to the demands of regular international football. Christensen returned to action vs Atletico Madrid. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Speaking at a press conference about Christensen’s situation recently, the Danish national team boss said : “I had a man on the phone who was almost in tears. “He has assessed that he isn’t ready for that. Consequently, he has withdrawn, concluding that, given his current state, his body isn’t prepared to play two international matches. It truly breaks his heart.” The meeting with Flick will provide an opportunity to coordinate the physical and sporting plans of Barcelona and Denmark. Christensen is equally keen to regain the consistency that injuries have repeatedly taken away from him. He remains a key figure for the Danish national team and continues to be held in high regard at Barça as well . As such, the planned meeting between Riemer and Flick seems like a sensible step, particularly given Christensen’s history of recurring fitness problems.

item.title: Justin Jefferson breaks down exactly how Kirk Cousins’ return will help elevate his game
item.description: Photo by David Berding/Getty Images With Kirk Cousins returning for the Minnesota Vikings, Justin Jefferson has explained why this should work out well for his production. One of the biggest issues with the Minnesota Vikings has been the lack of service to Justin Jefferson thanks to their issues at quarterback. Arguably the best wide receiver in the NFL, he has been severely impacted by their poor offensive play. But all that is about to change. Jefferson and Kirk Cousins had one of the NFL’s most productive partnerships during their time together in Minnesota, connecting for 5,396 yards and 28 touchdowns in the regular season. The wide receiver emerged as one of the best in the league when he was playing with Cousins. And now that the QB has returned, he explained why that will make a huge difference for him. Justin Jefferson highlighted Kirk Cousins’ understanding of how he plays and how defences play him Jefferson won Offensive Player of the Year after leading the NFL with 1,809 receiving yards in 2022, with Cousins slinging the ball to him. The two understand each other inherently, and it makes it very hard for opposing defences to cover Jefferson when there is that kind of a connection between him and his QB. That is exactly what the receiver highlighted at a recent press conference, explaining why he is excited about Cousins’ comeback. “It’s just kind of a joy to hear him take over and be a leader in the meeting room, on the field. It’s definitely a cool little situation, for sure,” Jefferson said about Cousins’ return. “He understands how the defences play, especially covering me. And he understands the plays that are kind of my plays. He understands the timing and the windows to throw those types of plays. But he also doesn’t force those types of plays to me, and he just lets the game come to me.” Considering how great the Vikings’ defence is, having Cousins potentially unlock Jefferson is something that the rest of the NFL should be worried about. Minnesota may well have found the perfect QB in terms of fitting their team as well as narrative to achieve the ultimate success this year. item.title: UFC boss White does not like Hokit's 'shtick'
item.description: Josh Hokit is fifth in the UFC's heavyweight rankings [Getty Images] UFC president Dana White says he doesn't like Josh Hokit's "shtick" but he has earned his heavyweight title shot against Ciryl Gane. American Hokit will face Frenchman Gane for the undisputed heavyweight title at UFC 334 at New York's Madison Square Garden on Saturday. Hokit is a controversial fighter, who in a similar vein to Colby Covington, adopts various personas during interviews to generate attention from fans. He has been accused of overstepping the line into discrimination, however, after making racially aggravated and misogynistic comments in his post-UFC 324 interview in January. After Hokit directed misogynistic comments towards former First Lady Michelle Obama in June, UFC president Dana White described his words as "gross", "moronic", and "inappropriate". Hokit directed more crude jokes towards his fellow fighters during a news conference to promote UFC 334, but White defended the 29-year-old. "You know how I feel about shtick, I don't like them, I don't like his shtick, but for anyone to say he doesn't deserve this fight is crazy," said White. "He earned this fight, that he absolutely did." Hokit will fight for the heavyweight title despite only making his UFC debut one year ago. Since then he has won four fights in the promotion, to extend his unbeaten record to 10. Some critics have argued he doesn't deserve a title shot yet in place of fighters such as Alexander Volkov, and he has been awarded it because his controversial comments generate attention. Gane, who is defending the belt for the first time since being upgraded to undisputed heavyweight champion in September when Tom Aspinall vacated the title , disagrees. "Honestly he deserves it, he's a great athlete, he's done very well, and he has a big mouth also that is good for the business," said Gane. "This is his character. I understand it, and I'm comfortable with it." Hokit poked fun at the 36-year-old Frenchman during the news conference by wearing goggles and an eye patch, in reference to Gane's fight with Aspinall in 2025. The bout ended in a no-contest after eye-pokes from Gane left Aspinall unable to continue. Aspinall later accused Gane of cheating, but the Frenchman says it was accidental. Gane consistently saw the funny side to Hokit's antics, as he laughed off the majority of comments from the challenger. "He's a smart guy, people underestimate him. He's a good fighter also, he's a good wrestler and I think he has a good fight IQ," Gane told BBC Sport. "He creates the character and that's smart, this is a business also. But he's not here only because of that that, he's also 10-0 and on a good run." It's an opinion Hokit agrees with. "Men lie, women lie, numbers don't, I earned my spot and this position, and I'm grateful for it," said Hokit.
